subject: Human Evolution
title: Discovery of the First Fossil
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Discovery of the First Fossil.

hook.text: In 1856, quarry workers found bones in Feldhofer Cave, Germany—and threw most of them away as rubble.

buildup.text: A local teacher rescued a skullcap and limb bones. Anatomists argued fiercely about what they were.

discovery.text: Some claimed the bones belonged to a diseased Cossack. Others recognized a new type of human.

twist.text: It took decades and more finds before the scientific world accepted Neanderthals as a separate species.

climax.text: That quarry find launched paleoanthropology—the entire science of studying ancient human relatives.

punchline.text: Bones tossed as trash founded a science.

quiz.question: Where was the first recognized Neanderthal fossil found?
